scientificRules: Preserve numerical precision, source measurements, units and references.
Preserve distinctions between measured evidence, modelled outcomes and planning assumptions.
All original source PDFs remain English-language scientific records.
Do not add certification, regulatory approval or universal validation claims.

terms.HPLC: High-performance liquid chromatography; preserve the established acronym.
terms.Mobile phase: Prepared liquid mixture pumped through the chromatographic system; not merely its neat-solvent ingredients.
terms.Mobile-phase recycling: Routing suitable prepared mobile phase back for reuse; does not mean purification or solvent distillation.
terms.Isocratic elution: Elution with a constant mobile-phase composition throughout the run; the intended application boundary.
terms.Gradient elution: Elution with changing mobile-phase composition; outside the stated ReSolve application scope.
terms.Acetonitrile: Chromatographic solvent; ACN abbreviation remains an invariant when used.
terms.Methanol: Chromatographic solvent; MeOH abbreviation remains an invariant when used.
terms.Analyte: Chemical component being measured in an analytical sample.
terms.Chromatographic separation: Separation of sample components through the chromatographic system.
terms.Retention time: Time from injection to elution of the selected analyte peak; preserve numeric measurement and unit.
terms.Peak area: Integrated detector response over a chromatographic peak; preserve original measurement precision.
terms.Resolution: Chromatographic separation between peaks; not display resolution.
terms.System suitability: Checks establishing that the analytical system meets the method’s agreed performance criteria.
terms.Detector signal: Measured detector output used to control routing, subject to assessed signal thresholds and timing.
terms.Waste diversion: Sending detected fractions and configured margins to waste; do not imply net annual waste prevention.
terms.Method validation: Documented assessment against intended analytical requirements; method-specific, never universal product certification.
terms.Analytical performance: Performance against selected method criteria such as retention time, peak area, peak shape and suitability.
terms.GMP: Good Manufacturing Practice. Preserve acronym; do not imply ReSolve is certified or grants compliance.
terms.Audit trail: Traceable record of events or changes; operating records and analytical validation are distinct evidence types.
terms.Hazardous solvent waste: Solvent-containing hazardous waste within the stated reporting boundary, including final disposal where relevant.
terms.Carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂e): Common greenhouse-gas reporting unit. The model’s source factors are locked assumptions pending verification; not measured emissions.
terms.Return on investment: Investment metric based on stated costs and benefits; gross material savings are not automatically net investment returns.
terms.Payback period: Time until modelled net cash benefits recover initial investment under stated assumptions; may be not reached.
terms.Measured routing recovery: Recovered flow divided by routed flow in the evaluated method. The study value is distinct from annual net fresh-demand or waste reduction assumptions.
terms.Net fresh-demand reduction: Separate planning input for reduced fresh prepared mobile phase. Include top-ups, losses and final disposal in site balances.
terms.Net waste reduction: Separate planning input for prevented waste; not the routing-recovery rate or an extra repeated-reuse multiplier.

terminologyReferences.use: Constant mobile-phase composition; phrased in our own words.
Changing composition during elution; outside current product scope.

translationDisambiguation.Sustainability versus stability: Environmental sustainability is distinct from chromatographic/analytical stability. Hindi uses सततता for environmental sustainability and स्थिरता for analytical stability; source-context checks must preserve this distinction.
